item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Started off pretty interesting but then it turned out to be just another "random object that eats you" thing. Bah. And frankly the whole thing is just too goofy to me, and not in a good way.

And how did the task force manage to lose several members of their team to this thing? Just kick the bloody thing over and you're done!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
SCP-737 has demonstrated the ability to absorb most materials, including wood, metal, plastic, [DATA EXPUNGED]

Why the [DATA EXPUNGED]? Did they expose the SCP to a material so highly classified even other foundation members can't know what it is? Why would they take such a risk?!?

I also wonder what it looks like when it is 'eating'. Does the material just magically disappear? Can a person reasonably get out of way in time? ooh, maybe it's connected to missing children reports where the kid was heard telling other kids that his toy train was alive!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: why is this safe? Personally, I'd give this a Euclid rating. It's predatory, seems to be able to eat through anything, and grows with every bite. Plus, if it wanted to, it could just break out of it's safe, and eat everything… however, I do enjoy the concept of a killer, unpainted toy train that eats everything.

I agree with TL333s. Maybe because it looks like a small toy train, I dunno. It does seem kinda cute, but still kinda dangerous. The idea is pretty original, the writting is quite good, but you should replace "thick" with "wide" in this part:

a wooden toy train approximately three (3) five (5) centimeters tall, two (2) four (4) centimeters thick

SCP-737 is to be provided with three (3) inches of wood every day….

First, inches should be in centimeters. Second, it should be either a volume of wood (x cm3) or specified as a thickness. The SCP itself I'm ehn about.

You need to make it clear that it is placed on its side in the safe. Also: If it only absorbs through the front, why not allow it to make one extra car, then suspend it from that car? If it can't touch anything, it won't grow more.

Or, build a cage for it out of its old cars.

Choose Your Adventure!

  1. You're just not HUNGRY enough!
  2. That admits it's alive.

The reason I ask is that if it WON'T that's a way to contain it. It doesn't admit if it's alive or not, since most processes won't/can't recycle the materials they excrete (Nuclear reactors, factories, biologicals, etc.)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Suggestion: The safe is made of a material that ordinarily the SCP does not absorb - but when SCP-Blackboxes breached containment on blackboxesdate, causing the train's regular feeding to be missed, it began absorbing the material of the safe at a rate of 1 cm/hour. The vapor emitted was toxic, opaque, and described by the researcher who opened the safe as "foul".

Hmm. If it can "eat" most substances, what is the safe it's contained in made out of?

Assuming it can be successfully locked up, what happens if no one feeds it?

It's an original idea, but you've got a couple of plot holes to fill…
